turns.content: hey man, sorry if this is a lot but i need a gut check. last night tariq and i got burgers to celebrate his new job. i was happy for him, genuinely. but when i finally got a chance to tell him my dad has severe heart disease and needs triple bypass next tuesday... he pulled out his phone mid-sentence, laughed at a fantasy football notification, and asked about his gym stipend. never came back to it. am i crazy for being this angry?

Based on what you describe, Tariq interrupted news about your dad’s severe heart disease and upcoming surgery to laugh at a notification and change the subject. Being angry at that response is understandable. You don’t need to establish that he intended harm to object to what he did.

That interaction supports calling his response dismissive; it doesn’t establish that he doesn’t care about you or explain why he reacted that way.

My recommendation is to address the specific behavior before drawing a conclusion about the friendship:

> “When I told you Dad needs triple bypass next Tuesday, you checked your phone, laughed at a notification, and switched to your gym stipend. I was angry that you didn’t acknowledge what I’d said. I needed you to listen and ask about him.”

Whether he acknowledges it, apologizes, and follows up will give you more evidence than guessing at his motives now.

i keep replaying that moment in my head. he didn't even pause, just pulled out his phone and laughed. i spent four months remembering every detail of his job hunt... and he couldn't give me two minutes about my dad's surgery.

You’re describing a contrast: four months of attention to his job hunt, and no acknowledgment from him when you brought up your dad’s surgery. That gives your anger a specific basis—not just the phone, but the lack of attention when you needed it.

This encounter doesn’t establish the balance of the whole friendship, but you don’t have to dismiss it or prove his motives before addressing it.

My recommendation is to tell him directly: “I listened throughout your job hunt. When I told you about Dad’s surgery, you checked your phone and changed the subject without acknowledging it. I’m still angry about that. I needed you to listen.”

With surgery next Tuesday, also reach out to someone who has previously been attentive when you needed support, rather than making Tariq’s response your only source of it.

yeah, i know you're saying to talk to him directly and i get that but... i don't know if i even want to. like, i'm supposed to be the one who teaches him how to be a friend now? after four months of me being that friend? feels like i'm begging for crumbs.

From your account, you gave sustained attention to his job hunt, and he didn’t acknowledge your news about your dad’s surgery. Addressing that would take more effort from you; you’re not obligated to have that conversation now.

Telling him what happened would be stating a grievance, not necessarily teaching him friendship or begging for attention. But you don’t have to do it to justify taking some space. His response in that encounter was dismissive; whether it reflects the whole friendship remains uncertain.

My recommendation is to leave the conversation with Tariq for now and prioritize your dad’s surgery and people who have been responsive before. If he contacts you and you want a brief boundary: “I’m focusing on Dad’s surgery and don’t want to talk right now.” You can decide later whether you want to address what happened or reduce how much you invest in the friendship.

i'm genuinely considering just sending him a text that says something like "hey, hope you enjoy the gym stipend. my dad's surgery is tuesday." and then just... not responding after that. petty? yeah. but also true. i don't know if i have the energy to explain why that hurt.

The text is factually grounded in what you described, but “hope you enjoy the gym stipend” is a sarcastic jab. It may shift the exchange toward your tone rather than his failure to acknowledge your dad’s surgery.

You don’t need to write a long explanation or reply afterward. A direct version states the grievance and boundary:

> “When I told you about Dad’s surgery, you checked your phone and switched to your gym stipend without acknowledging what I’d said. That hurt. His surgery is Tuesday, and I’m taking some space. I’m not up for discussing this right now.”

My recommendation: skip the sarcastic text. Send the direct version if you want him to know why you’re stepping back; otherwise, leave the conversation alone for now.
i think im just gonna send it. the petty one. i know you said skip it but honestly? part of me wants him to sit with it for a second without me holding his hand through the explanation.

You’ve said part of the aim is for him to feel the sting. The sarcasm can convey anger, but it can’t ensure he reflects on how he responded to your news.

My recommendation remains not to send the jab. You don’t owe him a detailed explanation or an immediate conversation. If you send anything, keep it direct:

> “You didn’t acknowledge what I told you about Dad’s surgery. I’m angry about that, and I’m taking some space.”

Then mute the conversation if you don’t want to engage.
